what_its_for: Naproxen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, reduce swelling, and lower fever. It is commonly used for headaches, muscle aches, backaches, menstrual cramps, toothaches, arthritis, gout, and minor injuries.
how_to_take: Take naproxen by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). It is best to take it with food, milk, or an antacid to help prevent stomach upset. Swallow extended-release tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Sit upright for at least 10 minutes after taking the tablet. Use the lowest dose that works for you for the shortest time needed.
dosing: For adults, the typical over-the-counter dose (such as Aleve) is 220 mg every 8 to 12 hours as needed. Do not take more than 660 mg in 24 hours unless directed by your doctor. Prescription doses may be higher and will be set by your doctor based on your condition. Always follow the label or your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you are taking naproxen on a regular schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store naproxen at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use naproxen past its expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking naproxen, as it increases the risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen, aspirin, or celecoxib) at the same time unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid lying down right after taking a dose. Limit activities that could increase your risk of bleeding if you are also taking a blood thinner. Tell your doctor before taking any new medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: stomach pain, black or tarry stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden weakness or slurred speech, swelling of the face or throat, skin rash or blistering, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), decreased or no urination, or severe headache. Also contact your doctor if your pain or fever does not improve after 10 days (adults) or 3 days (fever), or if your symptoms get worse.
when_it_works: Naproxen usually starts to relieve pain within 30 minutes to 1 hour after you take it. For conditions like arthritis, it may take several days to a few weeks of regular use before you notice the full benefit of reduced swelling and stiffness.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with extra caution. You may be at higher risk for stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and heart side effects. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time. Pregnant women: Do not use naproxen if you are 20 weeks pregnant or beyond unless directed by your doctor, as it may harm the unborn baby. Ask your doctor before use in early pregnancy. Breastfeeding: Small amounts may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using. Children: Over-the-counter naproxen (Aleve) is not recommended for children under 12 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution and only under medical supervision. Heart disease: People with heart disease or a history of stroke should discuss the risks carefully with their doctor before using naproxen.
